title: A critical U(2) suborbit gives an iid qutrit quantum-branch lower
theorem: For fixed 1/3<a<1/2, 0<c0<=c1<infinity and known p_n=(a+c/(2sqrt(n)),a-c/(2sqrt(n)),1-2a), an archive reconstructing the full unknown U(3) orbit in worst-case half trace with maximum branch dimension Q and arbitrary classical labels has e>=C r_n/Q for Q<=1/(32r_n), where r_n=c/(2a sqrt(n)); C depends only on a,c0,c1.
proof: Restrict to the U(2) suborbit on span(e1,e2), where each state is the flagged mixture (2a)rho_(r_n,v) direct-sum (1-2a)|3><3|. The n-copy qutrit family is exactly CPTP-equivalent to the variable-length qubit family direct_sum_M Bin(n,2a)(M) rho_(r_n,v)^tensor M by random flag-pattern embedding and flag extraction. Composition preserves Q and cannot increase worst-case error. Apply the critical-qubit bounded proper-score argument after Schur reduction. The score depends only on spin L, has global interval [-3/2,1/2], and every source/output spin pair has nonnegative deficit, with deficit >=c_B r_n/Q on source spins j=L/2 in [1/r_n,B/(2r_n)]. The M,L source and target baseline weights match exactly, so arbitrary changes of M and L sectors cannot cancel the score gap. Binomial concentration puts M in [an,n] with probability 1-o(1), and the critical qubit spin law has uniformly positive mass in the score band for every such M. Trace duality then gives the stated error lower.
costs: Converse allows arbitrary, including continuous, classical labels; arbitrary source/output copy-count and Schur-sector transitions; and unrestricted computation. No total hybrid dimension or alphabet lower is proved.
baseline: The critical-qubit rank-Q score converse in outputs/research/sol_collision_precision/quantum_branch.txt, §§2-7, plus exact orthogonal erasure flags.
falsifier: A valid qutrit archive in the stated family with Q<=1/(32r_n) and error o(r_n/Q), or a failure of the critical-qubit all-sector score inequality when applied to the variable-length direct sum.
unresolved_gate: This only gives Q=Omega(r_n/epsilon) below saturation. It does not recover the cold-mode epsilon^(-2) factor or prove the joint law Q=Theta(epsilon^(-2)max{1,r_n/epsilon}); multiplying subgroup lower bounds is unsupported. External validation and priority remain open.
